lines.spoken: Chapter 3: Software-Defined Networking Security and Network Programmability.

lines.text: 1. SDN and SDN Security
lines.spoken: 1. SDN and SDN Security.

lines.text: Why SDN
lines.spoken: Why SDN.

lines.text: Modern applications and the cloud add complexity, which leads to configuration errors, downtime, and security problems.
lines.spoken: Modern applications and the cloud add complexity, which leads to configuration errors, downtime, and security problems.

lines.text: Network infrastructure must keep pace with the business and help simplify the network.
lines.spoken: Network infrastructure must keep pace with the business and help simplify the network.

lines.text: Traditional Networking
lines.spoken: Traditional Networking.

lines.text: The control plane was always separate from the data plane, but there was no central brain.
lines.spoken: The control plane was always separate from the data plane, but there was no central brain.

lines.text: Each device had its own brain and did not share intelligent information with others.
lines.spoken: Each device had its own brain and did not share intelligent information with others.

lines.text: Devices were managed separately: CLI, GUI, Tcl scripts, and ASDM for firewalls.
lines.spoken: Devices were managed separately: CLI, gooey, Tcl scripts, and ASDM for firewalls.

lines.text: What SDN Changed
lines.spoken: What SDN Changed.

lines.text: Moved from a distributed "semi-intelligent brain" to a "central and intelligent brain."
lines.spoken: Moved from a distributed "semi-intelligent brain" to a "central and intelligent brain."

lines.text: The biggest change was in the control and data planes of software-based switches and routers, including virtual switches in hypervisors. The Open vSwitch project started much of this.
lines.spoken: The biggest change was in the control and data planes of software-based switches and routers, including virtual switches in hypervisors. The Open vSwitch project started much of this.

lines.text: SDN gives many benefits in the management plane for physical and virtual switches.
lines.spoken: SDN gives many benefits in the management plane for physical and virtual switches.

lines.text: SDN is now widely adopted in data centers.
lines.spoken: SDN is now widely adopted in data centers.

lines.text: SDN controller examples: OVS with OVSDB and OpenFlow, and Cisco APIC.
lines.spoken: SDN controller examples: OVS with O.V.S. D.B. and OpenFlow, and Cisco A-pick.

lines.spoken: A-pick Functions.

lines.spoken: Boot director: booting and firmware updates for spine switches, leaf switches, and A-picks.

lines.spoken: Appliance director: forms and controls the A-pick appliance cluster.

lines.spoken: VMM (virtual machine manager): agent between the policy repository and a hypervisor. Talks to systems such as VMware vCenter.

lines.spoken: Event manager: stores all events and faults from the A-pick and fabric nodes.

lines.spoken: Appliance element: inventory and state of the local A-pick.

lines.text: VXLAN and Overlays
lines.spoken: V.X. lan and Overlays.

lines.text: Modern data centers need load balancing, scalability, elasticity, and faster convergence.
lines.spoken: Modern data centers need load balancing, scalability, elasticity, and faster convergence.

lines.text: Overlay requirements:
lines.spoken: Overlay requirements:

lines.text: Separate tenant flows in the underlay.
lines.spoken: Separate tenant flows in the underlay.

lines.text: Switch within the same Layer 2 broadcast domain.
lines.spoken: Switch within the same Layer 2 broadcast domain.

lines.text: Route between Layer 3 domains.
lines.spoken: Route between Layer 3 domains.

lines.text: Provide IP separation.
lines.spoken: Provide IP separation.

lines.text: All tunneling protocols carry an Ethernet frame in an IP frame. They differ in the IP frame type: VXLAN uses UDP, and STT uses TCP.
lines.spoken: All tunneling protocols carry an Ethernet frame in an IP frame. They differ in the IP frame type: V.X. lan uses UDP, and STT uses TCP.

lines.text: UDP lets routers hash the outer UDP header to load balance with ECMP.
lines.spoken: UDP lets routers hash the outer UDP header to load balance with ECMP.

lines.text: The VXLAN source port is a hash of the inner headers, which adds entropy for ECMP.
lines.spoken: The V.X. lan source port is a hash of the inner headers, which adds entropy for ECMP.

lines.text: Traditional access-to-distribution designs block redundant links because of spanning tree.
lines.spoken: Traditional access-to-distribution designs block redundant links because of spanning tree.

lines.text: Overlays can provide Layer 2 capabilities or Layer 3 routing.
lines.spoken: Overlays can provide Layer 2 capabilities or Layer 3 routing.

lines.text: VXLAN frame flags: RRRRIRRR.
lines.spoken: V.X. lan frame flags: R R R R I R R R.

lines.text: Micro-Segmentation
lines.spoken: Micro-Segmentation.

lines.text: Old model: servers were assigned subnets and VLANs, so policy was tied to VLAN boundaries in one data center or campus.
lines.spoken: Old model: servers were assigned subnets and V-lans, so policy was tied to V-lan boundaries in one data center or campus.

lines.text: Applications now move between servers, data centers, and clouds.
lines.spoken: Applications now move between servers, data centers, and clouds.

lines.text: VLAN segmentation keeps policy in central firewalls, but most data center traffic is east-west and often never hits the firewall or even leaves the physical server.
lines.spoken: V-lan segmentation keeps policy in central firewalls, but most data center traffic is east-west and often never hits the firewall or even leaves the physical server.

lines.text: Policies should not depend on VLAN, subnet, rack, or data center, and traffic should not bounce back and forth to a central firewall.
lines.spoken: Policies should not depend on V-lan, subnet, rack, or data center, and traffic should not bounce back and forth to a central firewall.

lines.text: Containers make segmentation harder because they move and change more often.
lines.spoken: Containers make segmentation harder because they move and change more often.

lines.text: Micro-segmentation starts and ends with the application itself.
lines.spoken: Micro-segmentation starts and ends with the application itself.

lines.spoken: N.F.V. Infrastructure Requirements.

lines.spoken: A network controller to control all virtual forwarders.

lines.spoken: N.F.V. was created to fix inefficiencies introduced by virtualization.

lines.text: VNF Manager: lifecycle management of VNF instances. Coordinates configuration and event reporting between the NFVI and element and network management systems.
lines.spoken: V.N.F. Manager: lifecycle management of V.N.F. instances. Coordinates configuration and event reporting between the N.F.V.I. and element and network management systems.

lines.spoken: Contiv.

lines.text: Assigns an IP address to each container, so no host-based port NAT is needed.
lines.spoken: Assigns an IP address to each container, so no host-based port NAT is needed.

lines.text: Built-in east-west service load balancing and traffic isolation.

lines.spoken: Works with Kubernetes and Docker Swarm. Kubernetes provides compute, and Contiv provides networking.

lines.text: NETCONF

lines.text: Client is the management application. Server is the managed device.

lines.text: NETCONF came before YANG, but YANG is now the only widely used language with it.

lines.text: Session flow:

lines.text: Both sides send a hello with supported NETCONF versions. The server lists optional capabilities.
lines.spoken: Both sides send a hello with supported net-conf versions. The server lists optional capabilities.

lines.text: The client initiates all exchanges.
lines.spoken: The client initiates all exchanges.

lines.text: Messages are an RPC (request) or an rpc-reply. An rpc-reply can be an rpc-error.

lines.text: RESTCONF
lines.spoken: rest-conf.

lines.text: Follows REST principles, but not all REST APIs are compatible with RESTCONF.

lines.text: Five requests: GET, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE.
lines.spoken: Five requests: get, put, post, patch, delete.

lines.text: Shared with NETCONF: client-server model, layered system, and the first two uniform interface principles.
lines.spoken: Shared with net-conf: client-server model, layered system, and the first two uniform interface principles.

lines.text: Key difference is the stateless server principle. NETCONF uses sessions, so it is not stateless.
lines.spoken: Key difference is the stateless server principle. net-conf uses sessions, so it is not stateless.

lines.text: Every RESTCONF request is acted on immediately. Transactions cannot span multiple messages, so networkwide transactions are not possible.
lines.spoken: Every rest-conf request is acted on immediately. Transactions cannot span multiple messages, so networkwide transactions are not possible.

lines.text: The book also says RESTCONF "requires the server to keep some client state," which conflicts with the stateless point. Expect the exam to treat RESTCONF as stateless.
lines.spoken: The book also says rest-conf "requires the server to keep some client state," which conflicts with the stateless point. Expect the exam to treat rest-conf as stateless.
